subject: Re: Urgent: HorizonPay bakeoff — final benchmark & proposed continuity package
messages:
From: Luis Moreno <luis.moreno@horizonpay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: HorizonPay Procurement <procurement@horizonpay.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: HorizonPay bakeoff — immediate data request and timeline

Evelyn —

Thanks for staying on top of this. We just kicked off a competitive bakeoff between Redwood and RivalX. The procurement team is pushing a final decision window of Dec 10. Before that happens, they need two things from both vendors:

- A short, self-contained benchmark that mirrors our production traffic (session length distribution attached in the doc we shared earlier).
- A written continuity proposal that covers: committed throughput, fallback plan, and a commercial continuity package if we need assistance migrating to Redwood mid-contract.

Can you share a concise benchmark snapshot (p95 latency under 4k tokens, expected nodes to hit 90 req/s steady-state, and any quantization tradeoffs) by Nov 30? Also — can you commit to a continuity resiliency credit if we decide to transition mid-term? Procurement needs something they can include in the RFP addendum.

If it helps, I can jump on a 30-min sync tomorrow morning.

—Luis
Luis Moreno
Senior Cloud Architect, HorizonPay
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Luis Moreno <luis.moreno@horizonpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HorizonPay bakeoff — immediate data request and timeline

Luis —

Appreciate the heads-up and the timeline. Short answers up front: yes, we can deliver a benchmark snapshot by COB Nov 30 and we can provide a formal continuity package that includes a migration credit and guaranteed uplift capacity for a defined window. Details below.

Benchmark plan (what we'll deliver Nov 30):
- P95/99 token latency for the sample session profile you shared (we'll run at your median/90th % traffic split).
- Expected throughput (req/s) on dedicated G4-style node pool + quantized LLM variant; expected KV cache hit impact documented.
- Tail latency under concurrent bursts (10% headroom test).

Continuity package (outline — will send formal PDF):
- 30-day migration assistance credit (up to $40k) applied if HorizonPay initiates a mid-term move to Redwood Dedicated.
- 2-week guaranteed provisioning of burst nodes to cover +40% traffic spikes during migration window.
- Free managed roll-forward for the initial 90 days: one on-call runbook review + two playbook drills.

I've looped Karthik (benchmarks) and Marissa (commercial/save plan) to finalize numbers. We will attach the measured CSV and a draft continuity_package_v3.pdf by Nov 30.

If you want to take the 30-min sync, I'm available Mon 11/30 9–10am PT.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[attachment: continuity_requirements_example.pdf (reference)]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Luis Moreno <luis.moreno@horizonpay.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HorizonPay bakeoff — immediate data request and timeline (benchmark snapshot)

Luis / Evelyn —

We ran the first pass of the benchmark against a dedicated 4xA10x node pool (internal variant matching your cloud instance class). Key snapshots attached in horizonpay_final_benchmark_20261130.csv. Highlights:

- P95 token latency (4k median session): 220ms/token on quantized fp16 -> equates to average generation latency ~1.1s for a 5-token burst.
- P99 token latency: 520ms/token during a 15% concurrency burst.
- Sustained throughput: 95 req/s measured on a 4-node pool with 32-GB KV cache allocated (we saw linear throughput to ~120 req/s before queueing growth).
- Quantization tradeoff: INT8 gives 1.6x cost reduction with a measured ~3% drop in perplexity on your prompt set; we recommend INT8 for background inference and fp16 for critical flows.

Notes on configuration we used (short):
- Model: openbase-llm-7b (redwood-tuned) quantized -> INT8 and fp16 variants tested.
- Sequence profile: matched to your supplied session-profile.json (90% under 1k tokens, 8% 1–4k, 2% >4k).
- KV caching: warm-cache improves p95 by ~18% for repeated sessions.

Attachments: horizonpay_final_benchmark_20261130.csv (CSV of raw runs), brief runbook snippet included inline.

We can snap another run with your exact prod dataset if you can provide sanitized logs (anonymized request IDs).

—Karthik
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: horizonpay_final_benchmark_20261130.csv (6 MB)]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Luis Moreno <luis.moreno@horizonpay.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HorizonPay bakeoff — proposed continuity package and commercial terms

Luis —

Thanks for the quick run, Karthik — nice work. Following internal review, here's a concise commercial continuity proposition you can include in the addendum. I'll attach a redline of standard terms (terms_redline_hp.docx) and the formal continuity package PDF.

Commercial continuity package (finalized):
- Migration credit: $40,000 applied as account credit valid for 90 days post-contract execution if HorizonPay requests vendor-assisted migration.
- Performance guarantee: P95 token latency ≤ 600ms under the agreed profile for sustained throughput up to 90 req/s. If not met, automatic SLA credit of 2% of monthly committed spend per missed month (capped at 10%).
- Capacity uplift: guaranteed burst capacity (+40%) for 14 days during transition, with 48-hour provisioning SLA.
- One-time onboarding discount: 15% off first 3 months of committed Dedicated spend if you sign within 30 days.

We believe this package addresses the core procurement concerns: predictability, fallback support, and a tangible migration incentive. If procurement needs the DocuSign envelope for the continuity addendum, I've created a draft: https://www.docusign.com/share/0a1b2c3d4e5f

Next steps:
1) Procurement to confirm they want the continuity clause in the RFP addendum (Luis).
2) If yes, we finalize the DocuSign and include the benchmark CSV as an appendix.
3) Legal can redline the terms_redline_hp.docx — Naomi, please keep an eye.

Happy to jump on the 30-min sync Monday if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
[attachment: continuity_package_v3.pdf (interactive PDF)]
From: Luis Moreno <luis.moreno@horizonpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: HorizonPay Procurement <procurement@horizonpay.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HorizonPay bakeoff — acceptance of continuity language pending legal review

Marissa / Evelyn —

This is exactly what procurement wanted to see. They asked me to confirm two quick items before I include the continuity clause in the addendum:

1) Can the migration credit be used for professional services or only platform credits?
2) For the capacity uplift, can you provide an emergency contact and an escalation SLA for provisioning outside regular business hours?

If you can confirm both by EOD Monday (12/6), procurement will include the clause in the RFP addendum and proceed with a short legal review. Pending that, we expect the final vendor decision to be made by Dec 10.

Also — legal asked for the redlined terms doc (terms_redline_hp.docx). Please upload to our shared HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HP-2026-041

Thanks — I appreciate the speed on this.

—Luis
Senior Cloud Architect, HorizonPay
